data.title: NQ: Nasdaq Futures Jump 1% as Wall Street Returns from Thanksgiving
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq futures lead the rebound
  • Nvidia faces fresh export pressure
  • Higher yields test holiday optimism

Global stocks found some footing after a turbulent week. Recovery is still fragile.

📈 Futures rise after a wild reversal

  • Nasdaq futures gained 1% in early Friday trading, while S&P 500 futures advanced 0.8%. Wall Street returns from Thanksgiving with buyers apparently being thankful for these gains after much trouble earlier in the week.
  • Wednesday’s rebound extended beyond technology. The Dow recovered more than 1,260 points from its low to finish higher, while small caps also gained.
  • Today’s session is shortened, with US stock trading ending at 1 p.m. ET. Black Friday also puts retailers and consumer demand in focus.
  • Reduced holiday participation can magnify price swings, making the strength and breadth of buying more informative than an isolated jump in the headline index.

🖥️ Nvidia adds another complication

  • Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners to halt shipments of servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The development puts export access back in focus.
  • Server manufacturers also face scrutiny. Dell and Supermicro reportedly told affected customers that Nvidia would not permit their orders to ship.
  • Earnings continue to separate individual stocks. HP surged 11.5% after-hours Wednesday after beating expectations, while Amazon fell 3.1%. HP’s results benefited from tariff refunds, however, underscoring why a strong earnings reaction deserves a closer look at the recurring profits behind it.

🌍 Global relief meets higher yields

  • Asian equities advanced, with Japan’s Nikkei up about 0.7% and South Korea gaining around 2%. The US 10-year Treasury yield nevertheless rose toward 4.89%, while the dollar index hovered near 103.8.
  • Tokyo core inflation reached a 16-month high, reinforcing expectations of a Bank of Japan hike; USDJPY traded around ¥159.30. EURUSD held near $1.0980.
  • With a December Fed increase also almost fully priced, traders face a recovery unfolding against continued monetary tightening rather than imminent policy relief.
  • Gold rebounded 1.6% toward $3,620, while Bitcoin traded around $61,700. Brent crude hovered near $96, heading for its first weekly gain in four amid supply concerns.

data.title: Indian central bank lets rupee rise to break one-way bets on depreciation
data.description:
By Nimesh Vora and Ira Dugal

India's central bank is using the return of foreign inflows to break bets on a one-way slide in the rupee, allowing the currency to strengthen rather than buying dollars to rebuild reserves.

The strategy could encourage exporters to sell more dollars, reduce hedging by importers and ease foreign investors' concerns over currency losses, analysts and two sources familiar with the Reserve Bank of India's thinking said.

Indian equities have drawn a record $16 billion in foreign inflows in November, reversing nearly two years of selling and providing the central bank an opportunity to rebuild reserves.

Yet, the RBI has largely stayed out of the currency market despite an $80 billion drawdown in reserves from their $785.7 billion peak, following heavy dollar sales in October to defend the rupee as it approached its record low of 96.96 per dollar.

The RBI's dollar purchases during the rupee's recovery have been limited despite around $40 billion in forward commitments maturing over the next year, Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist and senior economist at ANZ Bank, said.

"We think its immediate priority is to put exporter hedging on a sustained footing and ease forward market imbalances (between importer and exporter hedging)," he added.

"That may require further rupee appreciation."

Nim said the rupee would face stiff resistance at 90-91 per dollar. The currency traded at 92.62 on Friday.

The RBI is in "no hurry" to rebuild reserves and could allow the rupee to appreciate while replenishing reserves if inflows persist, one of the sources said, requesting anonymity due to restrictions on speaking to the media.

The strategy is consistent with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's publicly stated view that the rupee was undervalued.

An RBI spokesperson did not respond to an email seeking comment on the currency strategy.

EARLY SIGNS OF RESET

The rupee fell 4.8% in 2025 and another 5.5% in the first 10 months of this year, pressured by nearly $50 billion in foreign equity outflows amid India's limited exposure to the AI investment boom and steep valuations.

Persistent weakness prompted foreign investors to build short rupee positions in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market, exporters to retain dollar earnings and importers to step up hedging.

The resulting spiral prompted the RBI to curb open currency positions, impose reserve requirements on large hedging transactions and allow oil companies to buy dollars directly from its reserves.

With the rupee now up more than 4% from its lows, expectations are shifting.

Exporter hedging volumes over the past week were significantly higher than levels seen throughout the year, the head of markets at a large private-sector bank said, citing renewed hedging of future dollar receivables by Indian IT companies.

Investors turned bullish on the rupee for the first time in 18 months, helped by record foreign equity inflows and lower oil prices, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.

FLEXIBILITY ON RATES

A sustained recovery in the rupee would provide the RBI higher flexibility to focus monetary policy on domestic growth and inflation conditions, rather than having to contend with currency weakness. This, in turn, could strengthen the rupee's fundamental support.

"Credible moves" on interest rates to address domestic sources of inflation would do more to ease underlying pressures on the rupee, said Aaron Hurd, senior portfolio manager for currency at State Street Investment Management.

"We need to see 2-3 more rate hikes over the coming quarters, preferably front-loaded with a hike at each of the next two meetings."

data.title: Thales in exclusive talks to buy controlling stake in laser tech firm Lumibird
data.description:
French laser technology company Lumibird said on Friday it had entered into exclusive talks with defence group Thales for the sale of a 51.6% stake held by its CEO and majority shareholder Marc Le Flohic.

The proposed price is €30.10 per share, including an exceptional distribution of €11.34 per share tied to the sale of Lumibird's medical division, which implies an enterprise value of about €440 million ($483 million) for Lumibird's photonics division.

Following the stake purchase, Thales plans to launch a mandatory simplified tender offer for the remaining Lumibird shares, including a squeeze-out if legal conditions are met.

The stake acquisition is expected to close by the second quarter of 2027, subject to the medical division disposal and regulatory clearances.

The proposed transaction has the unanimous backing of Lumibird's board, which will issue a reasoned opinion after reviewing a fairness opinion from independent expert Finexsi, Lumibird said.

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Likely Has Seen Cycle Peak — Market Talk
data.description:
0621 GMT - The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield may have seen its cycle peak, but it is too early to anticipate a sustained fall, SEB's Jussi Hiljanen and Filip Carlsson say in a note. "The bond rally since mid-November has been fueled by the equity sell-off, perceived risks of overtightening and lower inflation expectations," the strategists say. A stabilization in risk appetite could send yields higher again, while continued risk-off would support bond prices. "We are hesitant to bet on a sustained downtrend until closer to the policy rate peak," they say. The 10-year Treasury yield is up 7.4 basis points at 4.921%, according to Tradeweb. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0610 GMT - The new European Central Bank president is likely to act more as a driving force, similar to Mario Draghi, rather than following Christine Lagarde's consensus-oriented approach, Neuberger's Patrick Barbe says. European leaders have picked Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos to lead the ECB. "In practice, we believe this could make the ECB more responsive: it may tighten policy more quickly when inflation rises and ease policy more quickly when growth weakens," the head of European fixed income says in a note. Earlier reaction to rising inflation should lead to less volatility in interest rates, he says, also expecting the ECB to communicate more precisely and to continue relying on forward guidance. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0605 GMT - Neuberger continues to expect the European Central Bank to raise interest rates in December, and does not see any material change in the monetary policy outlook, says Patrick Barbe, head of European fixed income. "Market participants have almost fully priced in a December rate hike and expect the next increase in April 2027," he says. Neuberger expects fewer rate hikes next year than are currently priced in. Neuberger has made no material changes to its country or duration positioning, maintaining long-duration stance, particularly in Germany and the countries of Eastern Europe, Barbe says. Money markets price in a 91% probability of a 25-basis-point ECB rate hike in December, according to LSEG. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0514 GMT - U.S. and China's trade relationship is likely to stay stable in the near term, according to BofA Securities in a research note. "The unusually frequent meetings between the two leaders signal a shared interest in keeping tensions in check," the bank says. While the U.S. recently proposed new tariffs on China, the increase is still within the existing U.S. China trade framework, rather than a signal of renewed escalation, the bank says. BofA expects the current trade agreement to be extended as its base case. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

0431 GMT - The gauge for China's factory activity is likely to indicate improvement in November, according to Goldman Sachs in a research note. GS expects official manufacturing purchasing managers' index to edge up to 49.5 in November from 49.3 in October. A PMI reading below 50 signals contraction in activity. The improvement is supported by high-frequency indicators, such as steel production, which rose sequentially during the month, the bank says. It also expects the RatingDog manufacturing PMI, compiled by S&P Global, to rise to 52.2 in November from 52.0 in October, supported by stronger port activity in coastal regions compared with last month. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

0409 GMT - Japan's core consumer inflation, which excludes fresh food prices, is expected to hover near the central bank's 2% target in the six months through September 2027, even after accounting for the impact of planned sales tax cuts, SMBC Nikko Securities economists say. They project the gauge will fall below 1.5% in the second half of fiscal 2027. "While a consumption tax cut on food and beverages is expected to weigh on inflation from April 2027 onward, the pass-through of past import price increases to final consumer goods is likely to intensify through around next summer," they add. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

0404 GMT - Japan's nationwide core consumer inflation, which excludes fresh food, likely accelerated to 2.6% on year in November from 2.2% in October, mirroring the pickup in Tokyo, Barclays economists estimate. They maintain their outlook for nationwide inflation to gradually rise going forward, citing renewed increases in oil procurement costs. However, the economists note that companies are passing less of their higher labor costs on to consumers than in 2024 and 2025, meaning recent wage growth momentum is unlikely to generate meaningful second-round inflationary effects. Government data earlier Friday showed Tokyo core consumer inflation picked up to 2.9% on year in November from October's 2.6% rise. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

0400 GMT - The Singapore dollar strengthens slightly against its U.S. counterpart in Asia amid mild risk appetite. Asian equities are broadly higher Friday, tracking gains in U.S. stock futures as market sentiment around artificial intelligence stabilizes. Markets will be watching for commentary from the Federal Reserve after the latest U.S. PCE data, with money markets currently pricing approximately 69 bps of additional Fed hikes by mid-2027, UOB's Global Economics & Markets Research team says in a note. The U.S. dollar is 0.1% lower at 1.2893 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0306 GMT - Next week could be an important window to watch for clues as to whether the MATCH Act, which restricts semiconductor equipment and components exports to China, will be enacted soon, Bernstein analysts say in a note. The most prominent restriction under the Act could be of immersion DUV lithography tools from ASML and Nikon, which are essential for all advanced logic and memory chips, they note. "If enacted, it would impede China's ambition to expand capacity and impact all equipment companies' sales to China, not just ASML," they say. The biggest signal watch would be whether the final 2027 annual defense bill, likely released early December, includes the MATCH Act, Bernstein says.(sherry.qin@wsj.com)

0304 GMT - Singapore's manufacturing growth is likely to moderate in 2027 from this year's strong momentum, CGS International economists say in a note. Industrial production growth accelerated in October, driven by strong performance in the precision engineering segment. Ongoing artificial intelligence infrastructure investment and semiconductor demand should support electronics production, they note. However, the potential moderation in next year's factory output would reflect a normalization in global electronics demand and a higher base, they say. CGS International projects Singapore's manufacturing growth to cool to 7.0% in 2027 from its 2026 forecast of 10.0%.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0259 GMT - The South Korean won is poised to strengthen further against the dollar in 2027, says Chris Turner at ING. The Bank of Korea's notably upbeat assessment of the domestic economy, the prospect of another rate increase next year to match expected Federal Reserve hikes, and wider current-account surpluses bode well for the local currency, the global head of markets writes in a note. The BOK expects the current account surplus to reach $500 billion in 2026 and $540 billion in 2027--sharply higher than the record $123 billion surplus in 2025, he notes. The won is up roughly 7% against the dollar this year, outperforming its Asian peers. The dollar is down 0.2% at 1,341.04 won, FactSet data shows. ING expects the dollar to trade at 1,275.00 won in 4Q 2027. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)

0241 GMT - Asian currencies could be weighed down by artificial intelligence uncertainties, DBS Group Research's Chang Wei Liang says in commentary. A major U.S. AI chipmaker has reportedly halted all shipments of servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, he notes. "There are no other non-U.S. commercial alternatives for such AI chips," he says, adding that the move will have a major impact on Asean data center investments. The Malaysian ringgit and Thai baht are likely to further weaken if foreign direct investment into data centers slows markedly, he says. The U.S. dollar is flat at 4.1130 ringgit and little changed at 34.03 baht, LSEG data shows.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: SEBI eyes faster foreign investor entry, 3-day REIT listing; reviews IPO and broker rules
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is looking to reduce the onboarding timeline for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to five business days and cut the listing timeline for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) to three days from six days, Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday (November 27).

Outlining the regulator's next set of priorities, Pandey said SEBI is also reviewing the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) framework, the Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) framework and the rules governing SME initial public offerings (IPOs).

The regulator is exploring a graded compliance framework for stockbrokers and is reviewing the framework for short selling and securities lending and borrowing in the cash market.

Speaking about the way forward for capital markets, Pandey said markets and regulations must keep pace with each other and that SEBI needs to strike the right balance.

"Optimum regulation is what it is called at SEBI," he said.

Companies have raised around ₹9 lakh crore through equity and debt in the first seven months of the current financial year, Pandey said.

He added that markets need to remain fair, stable and trusted, and meeting this challenge requires constant calibration of regulations.

SEBI's regulatory roadmap: Key announcements

FPI onboarding timeline to be reduced to five business days

SEBI will further ease access for global investors and reduce the onboarding timeline for FPIs to five business days, Pandey said.

He also highlighted the simplified compliance requirements for low-risk FPIs, adding that 740 FPIs have registered under the SWAGAT framework.

REIT, InvIT listing timeline to come down to three days

SEBI is looking to reduce the listing timeline for REITs and InvITs from six days to three days, Pandey said.

LODR, ICDR and SME IPO frameworks under review

The regulator is reviewing the LODR framework, which governs disclosure and compliance requirements for listed companies.

It is also reviewing the ICDR framework, along with the regulatory framework for SME IPOs, he said.

Graded compliance framework for stockbrokers

SEBI is exploring graded compliance requirements for stockbrokers as part of its efforts to simplify regulations, Pandey said.

Demat 2.0 Phase 2 to enable secondary trading

Pandey said the second phase of Demat 2.0 would enable secondary trading.

Short selling, securities lending and borrowing under review

SEBI is reviewing short selling and securities lending and borrowing in the cash market, he said.

Corporate bond market-making framework

SEBI is working with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Finance Ministry on a market-making framework for corporate bonds.

Pandey also said index futures would add liquidity to the bond market.

Exploring a domestically governed AI framework

The regulator is exploring a domestically governed artificial intelligence (AI) framework for the securities market, Pandey said.

Risk-based regulation remains a priority

Explaining SEBI's regulatory approach, Pandey said the regulator has eased requirements in areas where risks are low and acted firmly where risks have increased.

He cited simpler compliance requirements for low-risk FPIs as an example of a lighter regulatory approach.

In segments where risks have built up, such as equity derivatives, SEBI has introduced measures in phases, he said.

Pandey also referred to the regulator's action against the publication of unregulated grey market premiums (GMPs) for IPOs.

He said wider market access must be accompanied by greater investor understanding.

The chairman urged industry participants to work with stock exchanges to help companies access public capital while recognising the responsibilities that come with listing.

He said SEBI would continue simplifying regulations, adjusting its approach and consulting stakeholders as markets evolve.

data.title: China markets surge as Beijing unleashes national team
data.description:
Chinese stocks jumped on Friday, heading for their sharpest one-day rise in more than two years after Beijing vowed to strengthen the role of the state-backed "national team" in helping to stabilise markets.

The Shanghai Composite index , lately languishing around 17-month lows, shot up about 3.3% in afternoon trade, while tech and AI indexes leapt even further.

The STAR semiconductor index (.CSI950125) jumped 15%, Hong Kong's technology index surged 6% and the yuan rallied. Here are what market participants are saying.

KENNY NG, STRATEGIST AT CHINA EVERBRIGHT SECURITIES INTERNATIONAL, HONG KONG:

"It's a shot in the arm for markets. Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south.

"It's obvious that A-shares have reached a level that's gotten the regulators' attention too — that sends the market a pretty clear signal.

"But there's a lot of news affecting the market ... and so I don't think the development from here depends entirely on this one factor."

KENNETH GOH, DIRECTOR OF PRIVATE WEALTH MANAGEMENT, UOB KAY HIAN, SINGAPORE:

"The move was to boost market confidence. The market is in a technical bear market and the national team wants to ensure the market stabilises and to prevent negative spillovers.

"It's positive in the short term but the sustainability of it will depend on other factors like consumer demand and confidence, as well as investors’ views of future prospects. Exports seem okay for now. But challenges remain, such as trade barriers and restrictions on trade."

WEI LI, HEAD OF MULTI-ASSET INVESTMENTS, BNP PARIBAS SECURITIES (CHINA), SHANGHAI:

"The recent massive surge in trading volume across Hong Kong and China markets signals a significant shift in sentiment. While debate persists regarding whether we have hit the bottom, the data suggests a highly constructive evolution in market dynamics.

"While the National Team provides the foundation, today's activity shows a healthy rotation toward growth ... we are seeing a transition from leveraged speculation to high-quality participation from institutional and industrial capital.

"This combination of reliable state support and growing organic demand creates a robust environment for long-term market recovery."

CHARU CHANANA, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST, SAXO, SINGAPORE:

"There is an increasingly clear signal that Chinese authorities are uncomfortable with the extent of the equity market selloff. State-backed buying alongside other policy measures signal a growing determination to stabilise markets.

"However, I would distinguish between a turning point in policy resolve and a turning point in market fundamentals. There is a difference between authorities putting a floor under the market and creating the conditions for a sustained bull market.

"A policy-induced bounce needs to evolve into a fundamentally driven recovery before we can confidently call it a durable bottom."

JASON CHAN, STRATEGIST, BANK OF EAST ASIA, HONG KONG:

"It's very rare that Executive meeting of the State Council would make such direct comments. Last time it happened was 2024 when they rolled out a liquidity support package.

"Authorities' determination to halt the slide is definitely there. But if you're asking whether this money alone is enough to really lift the whole market, I don't think it's that simple.

"To help markets stage a medium- to long-term upward trend, more practical support policies, whether for the economy or for certain industries, are needed ... I think they really need to follow up on these, instead of just paying lip service."

data.title: AirAsia delays staff salary payments to end of month, internal email shows
data.description:
Key points:
  • Malaysia-based staff will now receive pay at end of month from November to March, email shows
  • Airline cites a 'challenging environment' and asks employees for patience
  • AirAsia Philippines pilots file notice of strike after 90 retrenched, union says

By Julie Zhu and Rozanna Latiff

AirAsia has told employees it will delay salary payments to the end of each month from November through March, according to an internal email seen by Reuters, as the airline takes measures to conserve cash and its Philippine unit cuts jobs.

The email, sent to Malaysia-based staff late last week by Chief People Officer Muhammad Khurram Zia, cited the need for a "temporary operational adjustment" at Southeast Asia's largest budget airline, which like its peers faces higher jet fuel costs.

Salary payments during the five-month period would be made on the 30th of each month or the last day of February, the email said.

It cited a "challenging environment" and asked employees for "patience and flexibility."

The email's contents were confirmed by two people familiar with the matter. One of the people said AirAsia had previously paid salaries earlier in the second half of each month.

AirAsia did not respond to a request for comment.

The Iran war has sent jet fuel prices soaring, putting airlines worldwide under their worst financial strain since the COVID-19 pandemic.

US low-cost carrier Spirit Airlines collapsed in May, Latvia's airBaltic sought bankruptcy protection in September and Norway's Norse Atlantic suspended flights on Thursday as it looks for urgent short-term financing.

AIRASIA PHILIPPINES ANNOUNCES LAYOFFS

Shares in AirAsia, which employs about 26,000 people predominantly in Asia, have declined more than 70% this year as elevated fuel prices and foreign exchange losses squeezed its operations.

AirAsia Philippines said on Thursday it would reduce its workforce following sustained pressure on its operating costs, without specifying how many staff would be affected.

The airline said on Friday it remained fully operational and committed to serving the Philippine market. The planned workforce adjustment will not affect passenger flights, booking or other services, AirAsia Philippines General Manager and President Anna Victoria Lu said in a statement.

The AirAsia Philippines Pilots' Union filed notice of a strike after 90 pilots were retrenched, its president said in a video posted on social media on Thursday.

Philippine Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino confirmed receiving notice in a text message to Reuters.

AirAsia reported its third consecutive quarterly loss on Monday, though it was narrower than the prior quarter. Its cash and bank balances stood at 905 million ringgit ($219.93 million) as of September 30, down 5% from June 30.

In an investor presentation accompanying its results, the airline said it was taking measures to conserve cash, including suspending unviable routes and returning 25 planes to lessors.

It said more planes could exit its fleet in 2027, and a creditor restructuring was underway as part of a plan to reset the business before rebuilding in 2028.

AirAsia CEO Bo Lingam said on Monday that the third-quarter results suggested "the worst is behind us," while cautioning that fourth-quarter fuel costs were expected to rise further.

Malaysia's government has been weighing options to support AirAsia without putting public funds at risk, Reuters has previously reported.

The country's finance ministry said on Thursday that it would ask AirAsia for priority over other lenders and strengthen oversight of the airline's board and management if it decided to extend support.

($1 = 4.1150 ringgit)

data.title: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
data.description:
Key points:
  • Asian shares find footing after bruising month
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for weekly gains
  • Wall Street closed Thursday for Thanksgiving

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices rose on Friday, rebounding from a more than one-year low, as a US holiday lull calmed AI-driven market jitters and eased selling pressure on bullion.

Spot gold climbed 2.1% to $3,640.84 per ounce by 0609 GMT, after it had hit its lowest level since August 2025 on Wednesday following hot US inflation data that cemented interest-rate-hike bets.

Bullion is up about 3.1% so far this week.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 3% to $3,640.20.

"Although gold has attempted to stabilise following its recent losses, investors remain cautious. US holidays could limit selling pressure on gold as the selloff in technology stocks and the asset liquidations pause," said Ross Maxwell, chief strategy officer at VT Markets.

"However, the timing of any recovery will depend heavily on the direction of real interest rates, the US dollar and investment flows."

Asian shares were set to end a bruising month on a steadier note as a holiday lull offered some respite from AI jitters.

Wall Street was closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

The US economy grew much faster than expected in the third quarter, data showed on Wednesday, while inflation accelerated in October, reinforcing expectations that the Fed will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

The US central bank raised rates for the first time in three years in September.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.

China's net gold imports via Hong Kong rose 1.6% in October from the previous month, hitting their highest level since April, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department data showed on Thursday.

Spot silver climbed 6% to $43.96 per ounce, platinum gained 4.3% to $1,345.82 and palladium rose 4.3% to $910.93. All three metals were on track for weekly gains.

data.title: Exosens supports Germany’s Future Soldier program with advanced 5G night vision technology
data.description:
EXOSENS SUPPORTS GERMANY’S FUTURE SOLDIER PROGRAM WITH ADVANCED 5G NIGHT VISION TECHNOLOGY

  • Exosens secures a major order for the supply of 6,000 5G image intensifier tubes for integration into fused night vision binoculars under Germany’s Future Soldier program (IdZ-ES), supporting the Bundeswehr’s infantry modernization efforts
  • The order underscores the growing adoption of Exosens’ 5G night vision technology among European armed forces, reinforcing its technological leadership
  • Exosens strengthens its role as a key ITAR-free technology partner to NATO and allies, enabling the deployment of advanced night vision systems for augmented soldiers

Press release, Mérignac (France), 27 November 2026 – Exosens (EXENS; FR001400Q9V2), a high-tech company focused on providing mission- and performance-critical amplification, detection and imaging technologies, today announces that it has secured a major order for the supply of 6,000 5G image intensifier tubes for integration into fused night vision binoculars under the German Armed Forces’ Future Soldier program (Infanterist der Zukunft-Erweitertes System – IdZ-ES). Deliveries are expected to begin in early 2027 and extend over several years.

Led by Rheinmetall as prime contractor, Germany’s IdZ-ES program equips infantry soldiers with an integrated system of advanced communications, protective equipment and optical technologies. It is designed to improve how soldiers move, perceive their surroundings and operate together as part of a connected force. Night vision is an essential element of this approach, enabling field operations when visibility deteriorates.

By combining image intensification with thermal imaging while also displaying augmented reality information, fused night vision binoculars provide augmented soldiers with a more comprehensive understanding of their tactical environment. Exosens enables these capabilities by providing high-performance 5G image intensifier tubes forming the low-light imaging core of the devices deployed under the program, enhancing operational readiness.

“This major order demonstrates the growing adoption of our 5G technology among European armed forces as they strengthen their night vision capabilities. We are proud to support the Bundeswehr’s Future Soldier program with our most advanced image intensifier technology for integration into next-generation fused night vision binoculars. This underscores our technological leadership as the world’s largest supplier of ITAR-free image intensifier tubes, addressing dismounted soldiers’ growing need for mission-critical night vision capabilities in modern conflicts,” said Jérôme Cerisier, CEO of Exosens.

Exosens’ high-performance 5G image intensifier tubes deliver enhanced image quality, extended detection ranges and superior visual comfort, even in very low-light conditions. Exceptional contrast and sharper detail help dismounted soldiers detect, recognize and identify targets, better perceive terrain contours, and maintain situational awareness. These capabilities meet stringent operational requirements of next-generation night vision systems, enabling soldiers to operate more effectively.

Building on its technological leadership, Exosens combines field-proven operational performance, reliability and quality with scalable industrial capabilities to meet growing demand for advanced night vision solutions, driven by modernization programs undertaken by NATO and allied armed forces.

Financial calendar

  • 22/02/2027: FY 2026 results (before market opening).

About Exosens

Exosens is a high-tech company with more than 85 years of experience in the innovation, development, manufacturing and sale of high-end electro-optical technologies in the fields of amplification, detection and imaging. Today, it offers its customers detectors and imaging solutions such as digital cameras, ion, electron, neutron and gamma-ray detectors as well as image intensifier tubes. This enables Exosens to address complex challenges in extremely demanding environments by providing its customers with tailor-made solutions. Thanks to its sustained investment, Exosens is internationally recognized as a major innovator in optoelectronics, with production and R&D activities carried out at 13 sites across Europe and North America and more than 2,000 employees. Exosens is listed on compartment A of the regulated market of Euronext Paris (Ticker: EXENS – ISIN: FR001400Q9V2). Exosens is a member of the Euronext Tech Leaders segment and is also included in several indices, including SBF 120, CAC All-Tradable, CAC Mid 60, FTSE Total Cap and MSCI France Small Cap. For more information: www.exosens.com.
